---
title: Import and export
description: Add bounded CSV or JSON transfer to a resource without bypassing its policies.
kind: how-to
metaTitle: CSV and JSON import and export
---

Import and export are per-resource options. Each takes the file formats and an allowlist of fields.

## Export

```ts
resource(schema.users, {
  columns: ["email", "name", "role", "createdAt"],
  export: {
    formats: ["csv", "json"],
    fields: ["email", "name", "role", "createdAt"],
    maxRows: 50_000,
  },
})
```

Export is off until you set `export`. The toolbar's Export asks the server for every row that matches the list's current filters, search and sort, not only the page on screen. The server reads them through the same path as the list: tenant scope, the resource's `read` rule, and only the fields the user may read, so a `sensitive` field or one `fieldAccess.read` hides is left out. Soft-deleted rows are included only when the list shows them, which needs the `update` rule.

The file has the columns in table order, or `fields` in its order. Each entry in `fields` must be a column or in `expose`. CSV cells that start with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return get a leading `'` so a spreadsheet does not run them as formulas; a negative number such as `-123.45` stays as it is. Dates are ISO 8601. A money column that stores minor units, through `minorUnits` on its format or a `money` field, holds the amount in major units as a plain decimal with no currency sign: `5900` cents is `59.00`. Ids, references and enum values stay as stored, so a file imports back as it came out.

The file name says what it holds: `users-all-2026-10-09.csv`, or `users-filtered-2026-10-09.csv` when filters or search narrow the list. An export stops at `maxRows`, 10,000 by default; a capped file is named `users-filtered-first-10000-2026-10-09.csv`, carries the `X-Flowpanel-Export-Capped` header, and the admin tells the user to narrow the filters. Each export records one `<resource>.export` audit event when the download starts, and counts once against `rateLimit`. Rows are ordered by the list's sort with the primary key breaking ties, or by the primary key alone (every column of a composite key), so a file never repeats or skips a row between batches. When the adapter cannot see the key, the export is unordered.

The route is `GET <paths.api>/export/<resource>?format=csv`, with the list page's own query string (`f_<field>`, `q`, `sort`, `deleted`). `export` is a reserved name, so no resource or queue can take it.

## Import

```ts
resource(schema.users, {
  columns: ["email", "name", "role"],
  import: {
    formats: ["csv", "json"],
    fields: ["email", "name", "role"],
  },
})
```

Each row goes through the create path: validation, field access, scope, the adapter, audit and realtime. A read-only or role-restricted field in the file is rejected. CSV headers and JSON keys match field names. A `money` field, or a column whose money format has `minorUnits`, takes the amount in major units, `59.00`, as the export writes it.

Picking a file asks first: "Import customers.csv? 48 rows will be imported." After the import, a file whose rows were all accepted gets a toast. When some rows were refused, a dialog lists each one by its row number with the reason, in the same words as the form, naming each field by its label, and **Download failed rows (CSV)** saves those rows with an `error` column to fix and import again. The words come from `labels.importer`.

Import enforces request and row caps. Rejected rows are reported, and nothing is silently truncated. For a large one-off migration, use a background job instead.

Every option: [resource() reference](/docs/reference/resources).
